Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: The absolutive is zero-marked; the agentive marker le³³ marks only transitive A and Sa (agentive intransitive S).
curated_comment: Lisu, Dechang dialect (dech1234, ISO lis, Sino-Tibetan/Tibeto-Burman, Sichuan China) — Language and family corrected: original xlsx listed 'VERIFICAR (ficha dice dadi1250 Dadibi)'; PDF is Yu (2007), a comprehensive grammar of Lisu. dech1234 corresponds to the Dechang/Northern dialect. The language has an active-stative (split-S) system: le³³ marks transitive A and agentive intransitive Sa; non-agentive So takes zero (absolutive). Key corrections: GB409_2-4 changed '?'→1 (all persons confirmed in Yu 2007). GB409_15 changed '?'→0 (non-agentive So takes zero, not le³³). GB409_16 changed 1→0 (conditioning is agentivity/control, not topicality). GB409_19 changed 0→? (original 0 lacked citation; insufficient evidence for Dechang specifically). GB409_24 changed '?'→0 (nɛ³³ = LOCATIVE in Dechang, not instrumental; le³³=ERG, du³³=INST). Shares source PDF with hual1240 (both Yu 2007); separate CSVs because they are distinct glottocodes representing different dialect varieties. Glottocode dech1234 is correct; the previously proposed dadi1250 is Dadibi (Trans-New Guinea, PNG), an entirely unrelated language.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: All persons of pronouns have distinct ergative/agentive forms with le³³ in Dechang dialect of Lisu. Confirmed in Yu (2007). Changed from original annotation '?'→1.

Comment: All persons of pronouns have distinct ergative/agentive forms with le³³. Changed from original annotation '?'→1.

Comment: All persons of pronouns have distinct ergative/agentive forms with le³³. Changed from original annotation '?'→1.

Comment: Agentive/volitional A takes le³³. See examples (312), (228).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Non-agentive intransitive S (So) takes zero marking (absolutive), not le³³. The active-stative system distinguishes Sa (agentive, takes le³³) from So (non-agentive, zero). Changed from original annotation '?'→0.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: CORRECTED from original annotation 1→0. In the active-stative system, the conditioning factor is agentivity/control, not topicality. See example (3a-b): the split is between Sa and So, not between topical and non-topical A. Topicality does not systematically condition the presence/absence of le³³.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: Non-topical A takes le³³ as part of the active-stative system.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: Animate A takes le³³. See example (3a-b).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: Inanimate A: original annotation 0 lacks specific citation for Dechang; Yu (2007) does not explicitly address inanimate agents for this dialect. Changed from original annotation 0→? (insufficient evidence).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: le³³ in main clauses. See example (312).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Non-main clauses: insufficient documentation in Yu (2007) for Dechang dialect to confirm or deny ergative marking in subordinate constructions.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Ergative alignment conditioned by the active-stative (split-S) distinction: agentive/volitional Sa takes le³³, non-agentive So takes zero. The language follows an active-stative pattern.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: The ergative marker le³³ and the genitive marker are distinct.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: CORRECTED from original annotation '?'→0. In Dechang dialect, nɛ³³ is the LOCATIVE marker (Yu 2007), not the instrumental. The ergative/agentive marker is le³³; instrumental is du³³. ERG≠INST.
